text:
Situation: Dextrose monohydrate has been on the FDA shortage list since 2022-01-13 and remains current as of 2026-10-21. Corvale East holds 72 bags of 50 g/1000 mL dextrose 250 mL bags at 30.2 per day, providing 2.4 days on hand. Other East presentations range from 3.5 to 13.5 days. Corvale General holds 10.1 to 19.5 days across presentations. Corvale Lakeside holds 9 days of 50 g/1000 mL 250 mL bags.

Why (FDA record): FDA first posted the shortage on 2022-01-13. FDA inspection 975174 at B. Braun US Pharmaceutical Manufacturing LLC (FEI 2021236) received an OAI classification letter dated 2020-10-22, 448 days before the shortage posting. FDA inspection 1110899 at Hospira, Inc. (FEI 1021343) ended 2019-11-21, classified VAI, 784 days before the shortage posting. FDA inspection 1146372 at Bieffe Medital, S.A. (FEI 3005164365) ended 2021-04-22, classified VAI, 266 days before the shortage posting. FDA inspection 1152417 at B. Braun US Pharmaceutical Manufacturing, LLC (FEI 2021236) ended 2021-08-17, classified VAI, 149 days before the shortage posting.

Our position: Internal transfers can stabilize Corvale East within days. Two manufacturers not on the FDA shortage list today are available for purchase.

Recommended actions:
1. Transfer 89 bags of 50 g/1000 mL, 250 mL from Corvale General to Corvale East — approved by pharmacy director (transfer request).
2. Transfer 180 units of 70 g/100 mL, 2000 mL from Corvale General to Corvale East — approved by pharmacy director (transfer request).
3. Transfer 63 units of 50 mg/mL, 50 mL from Corvale General to Corvale East — approved by pharmacy director (transfer request).
4. Purchase from ICU Medical Inc. — approved by buyer.
5. Purchase from BECTON DICKINSON AND COMPANY — approved by buyer.

Not recommended: Delaying transfers while awaiting new supply; relying solely on Corvale Lakeside stock.
